A.O. No.524 of 2012
Hon’ble V.K. Bist, J.
 Mr Pankaj Purohit, Advocate for the 
appellant. 
 Heard. 
 Admit the appeal. 
 Issue notice to the respondents returnable 
within a period of six weeks. 
 Summon the lower court’s record. 
 List after lower court record is received. 
(Stay Appl. No.11695 of 2012)
 Also heard on stay application. 
 Considering the submission of learned 
counsel for the parties, it is directed that till next 
date of listing, execution of the award dated 
23.07.2012 passed by Motor Accident Claim 
Tribunal, District Judge, Pauri Garhwal in 
M.A.C.P. No.24 of 2010 shall remain stayed, 
provided appellant deposits 50% of the awarded 
amount within a period of six weeks. The amount 
already deposited under the statutory provisions 
shall be adjusted. 
 Registry is directed to remit the entire sum, 
deposited under the statutory provision, to the 
Tribunal concerned within two weeks from 
today. The amount so remitted by this Court as 
well as the amount deposited by the appellant in 
compliance of this order, shall be invested by the 
Tribunal in a fixed deposit so that it could earn 
interest and would be subject to further orders of 
this Court. 
 Stay application stands disposed of. 
 
 (V.K. Bist, J.) 
 30.10.2012

10 UKHC010004502012
AO No.524 of 2012
The United India Insurance Company Ltd. ....Appellant
v.
Smt. Damyanti Devi and Others .....Respondents
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
None is present for the parties.
In this appeal from order, arguments have 
already been heard and this matter is reserved 
for judgment. 
On behalf of the appellant, it has been 
argued that in the instant case, the deceased was 
the driver of the tanker owned by the 
Cantonment Board, therefore, he is not a third 
party in view of the law laid down by the Hon’ble 
Supreme Court in the case of New India 
Assurance Company Limited v. Sadanand Mukhi 
and others, (2009) 2 SCC 417. It is also argued 
that the claimants could have claimed 
compensation under the Employee’s 
Compensation Act, 1923 (“the Act”). 
This aspect requires more deliberations. 
What is the scope of Section 147 of the Motor 
Vehicles Act, 1988? What is the concept of the 
third party? And What is the applicability of the 
Employee’s Compensation Act, 1923, if any in 
such matters? Therefore judgment is not 
delivered and the matter shall be heard afresh on 
the above points. 
List this matter on 13.08.2026, for further 
hearing. 
 (Ravindra Maithani J.) 
10.07.2026
